//: Manual corrections to the derived keeper record. Data, not code, so that
re-running `npm run data` can never lose them.
Sleeper will not let a team attach a keeper to a draft pick it ACQUIRED BY
TRADE. When that happened, the league worked around it by drafting a
similarly-named scrub into the pick slot as a stand-in for the real keeper.
`scripts/derive.ts` rewrites these picks at load time: the pick becomes the
real player, flagged is_keeper. Everything downstream — the keeper resolver,
draft history, the keeper history page, player pages — then sees what
actually happened, with no special cases anywhere else.
The placeholders are listed in `ignorePlayerIds` so they vanish from the site
entirely rather than lingering as orphaned contracts and empty player pages.

placeholderPicks.note: DeVonta Smith kept at R5. The R5 pick was traded in, so Sleeper could not flag him as a keeper; Devin Smith was drafted into the slot instead.
Malik Nabers kept at R5 by Tyler Jung, who later traded him to Brendon Ng — the contract travels with the player. Same traded-pick limitation as above.

//contracts: Direct patches onto a resolved contract, keyed by player_id. Use only when a
substitution cannot express the correction; prefer fixing the source event.
